name: cocot
why: A code converter on tty from the Cygwin era; obscure and old-school, with unclear depth beyond conversion.

brief.what_it_is: cocot (COde COnverter on Tty) is a small Unix command-line filter that sits between a terminal and a program and converts character encodings on the fly. It takes a byte stream in one encoding, such as Shift_JIS/CP932 or EUC-JP, and converts it to the encoding the terminal expects, typically UTF-8 or CP932, in the other direction too. It is wrapped around a command, as in 'cocot ssh host', so it works with interactive sessions over ssh or telnet. The homepage describes Japanese-language use, and the options it lists (-t TERM_CODE, -p PROC_CODE, -i to disable ISO-2022-JP handling, -n to convert without a child process, -o LOGFILE to log output) point to that focus. The homepage text was mostly unreadable in my fetch, so this description leans on the parts I could read.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage says it exists because Cygwin is a UNIX-compatible environment that can run ssh and telnet, but Japanese text from a remote Unix host or a Windows-side terminal can come through in a mismatched encoding, and the author wanted a tool to convert between them. The author's changelog also mentions working from FreeBSD's script.c as a reference.
brief.how_it_works: cocot runs a child command under a pseudo-terminal and converts the byte stream in both directions between the terminal code and the process code. Those two codes are set with -t and -p, and the defaults were set at configure time (CP932 for the terminal, EUC-JP for the process, per the homepage). The -n option skips conversion and is intended for use with script(1). The homepage notes that on Cygwin, a terminfo entry for cygwin must be installed on the remote host for full-screen programs to work.

brief.install_notes: On Cygwin, download the prebuilt binary tarball (cocot-20100903-bin.tar.bz2, built for Cygwin-1.7) and run ./install-cygwin.sh, which installs to /usr/local/bin. Cygwin also needs libiconv (Devel category) and inetutils (Net category) from the Cygwin Setup package selector. On other systems, use ./configure, make, make install. The configure script accepts defaults for TERM_CODE and PROC_CODE. For a remote Linux host, install the cygwin terminfo entry as described above. Homepage notes this is for Cygwin 1.7 and that the author's build was verified on Cygwin 1.5.25, Mac OS X 10.5.2, Debian 4.1.1, OpenBSD 3.3, NetBSD 1.6.1, and SUA. I did not check the GitHub README for brew-specific install steps, and the GitHub README was just a copyright line.
brief.standout: It is a tiny, single-purpose pty wrapper for Japanese character encodings, built for an older Cygwin-era workflow. The homepage's changelog is itself a history of Japanese-encoding fixes, such as Unicode East Asian Width tables and the CP932 default, which is unusual for a tool this small.
brief.status: quiet. The homepage says 'Last Updated: 2010-09-03' and lists the 2010 build as the latest binary. The GitHub page shows a copyright line through 2017, which suggests the repository was touched later, but I saw no release or commit date. Treat it as unmaintained-in-practice rather than abandoned.
brief.caveats: Built for Cygwin 1.7 and older UNIX environments; the homepage's test list stops at 2008-era platforms. The homepage is in EUC-JP/Shift_JIS, so my reading of its Japanese text was partial and some option descriptions may be incomplete. License is a BSD-style license per the homepage ('see. LICENSE.txt'); I did not read the license file. The GitHub README I fetched contained only a title and copyright line, so I could not confirm current build steps or Homebrew-specific behaviour. The scout note's 'unclear depth' is fair: beyond the conversion itself there is little detail I could confirm.
